title: The School
dek: A school cut open: a classroom and the library upstairs, the corridor, the canteen and the gym downstairs.
frames: In the … there is / there are …

truefalse.s: The clock is next to the whiteboard.
There are two pupils in the classroom.
The ball is in the library.
The library is next to the classroom.
There is a globe on the bookshelves.
The cook is wearing a hat.
The schoolbag is on the desk.
A student is reading a book next to the computer.
One of the lockers is open.
The fire extinguisher is in the gym.
The PE teacher has a whistle round his neck.
The climbing rope is between the wall bars and the basketball hoop.
The menu is on the wall above the table in the canteen.
There is a map of the world on the whiteboard.

A1: What is in your classroom? Write five sentences.
What is in your schoolbag today?
What is your favourite room in your school? Why?
A2: Describe your school day, from the morning bell to the end of school.
Compare this school with your school. What is the same? What is different?
Write the school rules for the corridor, the canteen and the library.
B1: Should pupils wear school uniform? Give reasons for and against.
Describe your perfect school. What rooms and lessons would it have?
Write an email to a new pupil telling them what they need to know about your school.

rooms.ex: I go to school by bus.
rooms.def: A place where children go to learn.

rooms.ex: Our classroom is on the first floor.

rooms.def: A room with lots of books that you can read or borrow.
A long passage in a building with doors to rooms.

rooms.ex: We eat lunch in the canteen at half past twelve.
rooms.def: The room where you have lunch at school.

rooms.ex: We have PE in the gym on Tuesdays.
rooms.def: A big room for sport and exercise.

rooms.ex: The children are playing football in the playground.
rooms.def: The place outside a school where children play.

parts.ex: The teacher wrote the new words on the whiteboard.
parts.def: A white board on the wall that the teacher writes on.

parts.ex: Our English teacher is really funny.
parts.def: A person whose job is to teach.

parts.ex: There are 25 pupils in our class.
parts.def: A child who goes to school.

parts.ex: Sit down at your desk, please.
parts.def: A table you sit at to read, write or work.

parts.ex: Push your chair in when you leave.
parts.def: A seat for one person, with a back.

parts.ex: Open your books at page 20.
parts.def: Pages with words or pictures, inside a cover.

parts.ex: You can't use a calculator in this test.
parts.def: A small machine that does sums.

parts.ex: Write the new words in your notebook.
parts.def: A book with empty pages for writing in.

parts.ex: I've got two pencils and a rubber in my pencil case.
parts.def: A small bag or box for pens and pencils.

parts.ex: Draw a line with your ruler.
parts.def: A long flat piece of plastic or wood for measuring and drawing straight lines.

parts.ex: My schoolbag is so heavy today!
parts.def: A bag for carrying your books to school.

parts.ex: Can you find Australia on the map?
parts.def: A picture of the land and the sea, showing where places are.

parts.ex: Look at the clock - five minutes to the bell!
parts.def: A thing on the wall that shows the time.

parts.ex: The marker has run out - have you got another one?
parts.def: A thick pen for writing on a whiteboard.

parts.ex: The dictionaries are on the bookshelves by the window.
parts.def: Shelves for books.

parts.ex: You can borrow three books for two weeks.
parts.def: More than one book.

parts.ex: Spin the globe and find your country.
parts.def: A ball with a map of the world on it.

parts.ex: You can use the computers in the library after school.
parts.def: An electronic machine for writing, searching and saving things.

parts.ex: A student is reading in the library.
parts.def: A person who is studying.

parts.ex: Can I open the window? It's hot in here.
parts.def: An opening in a wall with glass, to let in light.

parts.ex: I left my PE kit in my locker.
parts.def: Small metal cupboards with locks, where pupils keep their things.

parts.ex: The timetable is on the noticeboard.
parts.def: A board on the wall where people put up information.

parts.ex: There's a fire extinguisher at the end of every corridor.
parts.def: A red metal container that sprays water or foam onto a fire.

parts.ex: The school cook makes the best pizza!
parts.def: A person who cooks food.

parts.ex: Take a tray and go along the counter.
parts.def: A long table in a shop or canteen where food is served.

parts.ex: Put your plate and your drink on a tray.
parts.def: A flat board with edges, for carrying food.

parts.ex: What's on the menu today?
parts.def: A list of the food you can have.

parts.ex: Can you climb to the top of the rope?
parts.def: A thick rope hanging from the ceiling, for climbing.

parts.ex: She threw the ball through the hoop.
parts.def: A metal ring with a net that you throw the ball through.

parts.ex: Throw the ball to me!
parts.def: A round thing that you throw, kick or hit in games.

parts.ex: Do the exercise on the mat.
parts.def: A thick soft piece of material on the floor, for jumping and exercises.

parts.ex: Our PE teacher made us run ten laps.
parts.def: The teacher who teaches sport (PE = physical education).

parts.ex: The game starts when the teacher blows the whistle.
parts.def: A small thing you blow to make a loud high sound.

parts.ex: When the bell rings, it's break time.
parts.def: A metal thing that rings to show that a lesson starts or ends.

parts.ex: The school bus comes at eight o'clock.
parts.def: A bus that takes children to and from school.

parts.ex: We sat on a bench in the playground.
parts.def: A long seat for two or more people, often outside.

parts.ex: There's a big tree next to the playground.
parts.def: A tall plant with a trunk, branches and leaves.
